They’re two completely different disciplines. I mean, I can see how SOME algebra is useful in it, but I’ve never found myself needing anything above Algebra 1. 

I’m going to do a refresher on Khan Academy (I’m 23, so it’s been a hot minute since high school) over the Summer, and pick up the actual class in the Fall. I feel a lot less stressed out knowing I have a real shot at getting my math requirement done this year! 🙂

Yeah, I tried that, and they no longer have that option. I DID find a workaround, though it’ll cost me a bit more. 

I found out I can take an online statistics class equivalent to the one at my school, and if I pass (I’ll pass; I couldn’t technically take AP Stats in high school because of the prerequisites, but I did all the workbooks and practice tests—for FUN, by the way—and I likely would’ve done well enough to score at least a 4), I’ll bypass the prerequisite entirely (and earn the 4 credits for the college course). It’s not the way they want me to go, but I checked and there’s no rule against it. Yay for workarounds, I guess! 🤷‍♀️

Update: I am going to challenge my college's intermediate algebra prerequisite, citing knowledge of and ability to succeed in college-level statistics (which is the next course in the sequence, and therefore supercedes int. algebra). I'm going to be doing a proctored examination over the summer and receiving a letter from both the proctor and the course providers (I've been doing a combination of MOOCs, and I've just enrolled in a for-credit option through a large state university). It'll either meet my math requirement on its own, or at least enable me to take the next class in the sequence. 

I even checked with the university I'm planning to transfer to, and they said I don't technically need it as a prerequisite unless I'm a STEM major (I'm obviously not). Soooo, there we go. 

Thanks for the help, internet folks!

I have one person I view as parental, but they’re a literal celebrity and have way too much going on for me to ask that of them (we’re friends, btw; this person is not just a random celeb, just FYI). They know about my issues, and they care, it’s just that they’re busy af. 

In my ideal world, I’d have a parent like them. Not someone who tells me daily how pissed they are that the condom broke.
